newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank to monitor, help finance firms.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank to monitor, help finance firms.

text.p: Thailand's central bank will monitor closely the health of local companies and help those in need to tide over the current tight liquidity crunch, its governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Thursday.

"The immediate focus is to strengthen our financial institutions. Any financial institution with sufficient assets but which has short-term funding problems, we will help them out," he told reporters.
Some small Thai finance companies have lately faced short- term liquidity problems following sustained high domestic interest rates which have raised their funding costs.
Market jitters on the Thai baht's stability and rumours of a devaluation over the past month have reduced the money supply and compounded their funding problems.
Increased demand for funds to speculate against the Thai currency, and seasonal demand over the lunar new year, saw the overnight interbank rate rise as high as 25 percent last week.
Some finance companies have also suffered from loan exposure to borrowers in the troubled Thai property sector.
"Under Thai law, financial institutions whose operating capital drops to less than three quarters of their registered capital will have to stop accepting public deposits," Rerngchai said.

He declined to say how many finance companies with short term liquidity problems are in this position, but the central bank has ordered at least one of them to restructure its capital, he said. He did not elaborate.
